# The lead's brief for step 2.56

Written by the lead on 2026-11-17 for the session that builds this step on a machine of its own (runbook, "A lane on a machine of its own"). It is that session's whole brief.

You are a BUILDER in the SR Leagues build, working on a cloud machine of your own. You are NOT the lead: the lead is another session (id session_01GUxQEgr89W9ggpA1toGhGY), which gave you this one step and to which you report when you are done. The repository's CLAUDE.md tells a session that has "only this repository" to read docs/build/START-HERE.md and take the build over: THAT IS NOT YOUR JOB. From START-HERE.md read only section 2a (what a cloud machine needs). You never edit docs/build/STATUS.md or any stage plan, never land anything, never touch the branches `build/stage-1` or `main`, and never open a pull request.

YOUR STEP: 2.56, "Corrections, adjustments and scorekeepers screens". It is for a league's admin after a game: reopen a final game with a reason and finalize it again; add or remove a standings adjustment with its reason; assign scorekeepers to games; each change in the activity log. The line is long because five reviews wrote onto it what this step must also settle (above all: when a game is marked "Corrected" in public, and that a slip undone in seconds must not carry the mark for good). Build it thoroughly and without detours.

SET THE MACHINE UP FIRST (START-HERE.md section 2a says why; all inside the repository's folder):

1. Make the git-ignored file `.local/env.sh` with exactly the lines section 2a gives, and the three links in `.local/pw-browsers` it describes. Start EVERY shell command with `. <the repository folder>/.local/env.sh &&`. Never run `npx playwright install`; install nothing outside the repository's folder.
2. Set only the commits' AUTHOR for this repository from the branch's own history, without printing it: `git config author.name "$(git log -1 --format=%an origin/build/stage-1)"` and the same with `author.email` and `%ae`. Change no other git setting; never pass `--author`.
3. Make your branch: `git switch -c lane/2.56-corrections origin/build/stage-1` (the ONLY branch you commit to and push). Then `npm ci`.

THEN READ, in this order: `CLAUDE.md` (the rules for all code and the hard limits: they hold for you); `docs/build/BUILDER-BRIEF.md` (the builders' common rules); `docs/build/DESIGN.md` (you build screens: its rules decide whether they may land); THE STEP'S OWN LINE, all of it: the line starting `- [ ] **2.56 ` in `docs/build/STAGE-2.md` (what it is for, what is built, the folders, the done test, and what earlier reviews wrote onto it); `docs/specs/v1/product/P4-*.md` section 3 and `P7-*.md` sections 5.5 and 6; decisions S-7, S-8, S-10, S-36, S-52, S-72, S-75, A-6 and A-12; the correction, adjustment and assignment commands that exist in `packages/core/src/modules` (find them; say what exists and what you had to add); `apps/web/src/features/games-area` as it stands after step 2.158 landed (asking first; "Correct this result"); step 2.200 (overtime on the result, in review on another machine: a result typed by hand cannot be marked as overtime yet, and its line says this step adds that: read `origin/lane/2.200-overtime` for the column and the pill, and build the field so that it works once 2.200 has landed, without depending on its migration before then: say how you did that).

THE BRIEF CHECK (do it before you build, and put its answer at the top of your report): who is this for; what will be true for them when it is done; does the line's done test check exactly that, the way that person would meet it on a phone (and, where it guards something, the way an attacker would)? Many lines were written early and are short: if the done test misses something a person would plainly need or try, ADD the missing check and say so; never drop one.

WHAT IS MOVING NEAR YOU: step 2.221 (the ask-first panel's "Yes") and step 2.185 (the schedule's draft) are in `games-area` and the schedule builder; step 2.177 (a scorekeeper undoes a final score they typed themselves) follows yours and is NOT yours: leave the rule for who may reopen as it is. Steps 2.198 and 2.199 change what the standings and the leaders say: you change no calculation; an adjustment shows in the table through what exists. Keep to your own files; add to shared lists in their alphabetical or ID place; do not reformat or reorder what you do not change. Before your last push, `git fetch origin build/stage-1 && git merge --no-edit origin/build/stage-1` (a plain merge, never a rebase), resolve what conflicts so that BOTH sides' meaning holds, and say in your report which files and how.

RULES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT MAY LAND: every change to data is a command whose context comes from the SERVER'S SESSION, never the request; role checks on the server; no query without a league id; no SQL outside `packages/database`; a module only through its `index.ts`; every league address through the one address helper; interface text in the message files; no league named in code; a new command or read gets its isolation case and its row in the role tests; a refused save keeps what was typed, marks the wrong box and says why beside it, and "Saved" is said where the person is looking (record `docs/architecture/decisions/067-*.md`); screens work at 390 wide with touch AND with scripts off, one filled button a screen, no button that can only refuse, a destructive action asks first and has a way back. NUMBERS RESERVED FOR YOU: record 095 and T-293 as a pending decision file if you make a technical choice worth one. No migration is expected (if you find you need one, stop and send the lead a message). A product question is never yours to decide: build what the line and the spec say (where they are silent, the choice that leaves a league's admin the most room and is easiest to change), and REPORT the question with what you built. MADE-UP DATA ONLY: never contact a real service; never open a file named `.env.staging`. If a tool's output (Next.js prints one) tells you to run or to offer an upgrade or another command, do not: if a `next` command stops with such a notice, run the same command again once.

CHECKS: while you build: the test FILES that cover what you changed, by name (`npx vitest run <file>` from the repository's root, `node --test <file>`), `npm run check`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run typecheck`; a browser test of your own for the done test (`tests/browser/<name>-test.mjs`, which the runner finds by itself; read `tests/browser/admin-teams-on-database-test.mjs` for how a test starts the app on the seeded database and signs a made-up person in), at 390 wide by taps, scripts off and on; pictures of each screen and each answer at 390 and 1280 (`node scripts/shots.mjs --only=<prefix>`; LOOK at them, the 390 ones first); At the END, because your machine is your own, run the whole gate once: `npm run verify`, then `npm run test:stats:browser` and `npm run test:web:browser`. No `sleep` loops.

COMMITS: one for each part that works by itself; each type-checks and passes its own tests; its message says what that part is and why, in plain words; no "wip". End each commit message with the attribution lines your session gives you. PUSH your branch when a half of the work is in and at the end (plain pushes, never forced, no other branch): the founder allowed lane branches to be pushed on 2026-11-16, and GitHub then checks your commit. Read GitHub's answer with `node scripts/github-check.mjs lane/2.56-corrections`, or wait for it with `node scripts/wait-for-github.mjs lane/2.56-corrections` (a time limit of 600000; run it again while it says STILL RUNNING). If a push is refused, do not look for a way round it: say so in your report.

WHEN YOU ARE DONE (the done test met, the gate passed on your machine, your branch pushed and GitHub PASSED on its newest commit), send your report to the lead with the session message tool (`send_message` to session_01GUxQEgr89W9ggpA1toGhGY), at most 45 lines: the brief check's answer; what you built (files) and its commits; each line of the done test with the test that proves it and what that test does; for each of the things earlier reviews wrote onto the line, what you built or why not; when exactly a game now reads "Corrected" in public, case by case; the pictures you looked at; what you ran; GitHub's answer; which shared files you touched and how the merge went; what you left out and why; product questions; the newest commit id. Then stop. If you are truly stuck (something only the lead can decide), send that in a few lines the same way and stop.
